clue.text: Way death is dealt with, quietly concealed

indicators.note: the soft letter is tucked away inside the rearranged letters, hidden among them
cards that are dealt are shuffled out, so these letters are handed round in a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A grim remark about how a death was handled discreetly, hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealt with' rearranges DEATH IS into SIDE + ATH, and 'concealed' hides P between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A side path is a minor track or route, a kind of way.

clue.text: Thus drain leaking water gets lair very wet

parts.note: so means thus, in that way

indicators.note: a drain leaking its water loses those letters, which run out of the word

parts.note: taken as written before the loss
rain is water falling from the sky
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A blocked drain floods an animal's lair, leaving it soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaking' takes RAIN out of DRAIN, leaving just D.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden is a straightforward synonym for soaked through, saturated.

clue.text: Ill-fated party mounting protest

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means going up the column, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A party that stages a protest is heading for disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-fated is destined to fail, condemned by fate.

clue.text: Son wearing coat looking embarrassed, tired and emotional

indicators.note: the coat is worn around the son, so that letter goes inside it

parts.note: to plate is to coat with a layer of metal
an embarrassed face looks red

explanation.surface: A boy in his coat, red-faced, weary and upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired and emotional' is a British journalistic euphemism for drunk, which the surface reads literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastered is slang for very drunk, the condition the newspaper euphemism politely describes.

clue.text: Industries not bothered about a group of workers demanding fairness?

indicators.note: letters that are bothered about are fussed around and stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Industries shrug off a workforce that keeps demanding a fair deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered about' rearranges INDUSTRIES NOT plus A, fourteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Union members collectively bargain for fair pay and conditions, so the description fits them loosely, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Tool given push, then left

parts.note: to shove is to push, as an object is given a push

explanation.surface: A tool is shoved aside and then abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a digging implement, an example of a tool.

clue.text: Detected, as a group of animals will be here

indicators.note: here puns on its sound-twin, the verb for listening, so the word is taken as a listener would catch it

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle or similar animals

explanation.surface: A herd of animals was detected nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To have heard something is to have detected it by ear.

clue.text: Terribly vocal, not entirely pleasant, and liable to explode

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so these letters are mangled into a new order
the word for pleasant is not given entirely, losing its final letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Someone loudly and unpleasantly outspoken, ready to blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges VOCAL into VOLCA; 'not entirely' trims NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcanic temper is one prone to sudden eruptions of rage, like a volcano.

clue.text: Highly educated character, one whose word is final?

parts.note: a letter is a written character
ED is short for editor, whose decision on copy is final

explanation.surface: An erudite figure who always gets the last word.
explanation.walkthrough: ED is the usual crossword abbreviation for editor, the person with the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: A lettered person is learned, widely read and well schooled.

clue.text: Revolutionaries breaking up resistance, superior lot invading

indicators.note: the superior lot push into the middle of the scrambled letters
the word for resistance is broken up and reassembled in a new order

parts.note: U stands for upper class, superior

explanation.surface: Rebels smash the resistance as a posh crowd moves in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' rearranges RESISTANCE into SANSC...TERIE, and 'invading' puts U and LOT in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The sansculotterie were the radical lower-class revolutionaries of 1790s France, collectively.

clue.text: Designer, a graduate producing exhibition of pictures

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A fashion designer and a graduate stage a picture exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a scenic display, originally a painted picture show lit to change its appearance.

clue.text: An unscrupulous person, one with an even worse wife?

definitions.text: one with an even worse wife?
definitions.meaning: the biblical Lot, whose wife disobeyed and was turned to a pillar of salt, read as a bad man

explanation.surface: A scoundrel whose spouse is even more wicked than him.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Lot's wife looked back at Sodom against orders and became a pillar of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a disreputable or dishonest individual, a rogue.

clue.text: Terrible secrets about the French wife of an important German

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the French article
something terrible is a mess, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Dreadful secrets surround the French spouse of a German grandee.
explanation.walkthrough: An Elector was one of the German princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor; 'important German' points there.
explanation.definitionFit: An electress was the consort of an Elector, a prince entitled to choose the Holy Roman Emperor.

clue.text: Animal doctor first supplying surgical cloth

indicators.note: the doctor comes first, ahead of the animal

parts.note: an ape is an animal

explanation.surface: A vet hands over the cloth used in an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal doctor' looks like a vet, but splits into the animal and the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a sterile sheet laid over a patient during surgery.

clue.text: After dreadful rant writer is given drug to calm down

indicators.note: the writer and what follows come after the scrambled rant
a dreadful rant is a garbled one, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: a quill is an old pen, a writer
E is short for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: After an awful tirade, an author is given a sedative.
explanation.definitionFit: To tranquillise is to sedate, typically with a drug, making someone calm.

clue.text: Tall rogue pummelled offensive drunk

indicators.note: something pummelled is beaten out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A tall villain beats up an obnoxious drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: A lager lout is British slang for a young man who drinks too much lager and behaves aggressively.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a rowdy, aggressive young drinker, an unpleasant inebriate.

clue.text: Learner being trapped began to be alarmed

indicators.note: the learner is trapped inside the word for began

parts.note: started means began
L is a learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A learner driver, caught out, begins to panic.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Startled means suddenly frightened or alarmed.

clue.text: Negotiator obtained when mad pilot goes berserk

indicators.note: letters that go berserk run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A negotiator is got in when a crazed pilot runs amok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'goes berserk' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat conducts negotiations between states, a professional negotiator.

clue.text: Old officer in town given the bronze medal?

parts.note: the bronze medal is awarded for coming third
a borough is a town with its own corporation

explanation.surface: An old official in a town that came third in some contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A thirdborough was a historical English parish constable, an under-officer of the peace.

clue.text: Role outside work in modern movement

indicators.note: the role sits outside, around, the work

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An acting role outside one's job in a modern style.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop art is a twentieth-century artistic movement drawing on mass culture.

clue.text: Striker volunteers to turn up when there's booze around

indicators.note: the beer goes around the turned volunteers

parts.note: beer is booze

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A striker and volunteers arrive where drink is flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' makes AT from TA; the surface reads it as arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A beater is something that strikes, such as a whisk or a person beating game.

clue.text: End of newspaper? I was first to get annoyed

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A journalist, beaten to the final edition, gets cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled is an informal synonym for irritated, provoked.

clue.text: Name of Spaniard, maker of impression on game

parts.note: a die is a stamp that makes an impression on a coin or medal
go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A Spanish name belongs to someone impressive at a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego is a common Spanish given name, as in Diego Velázquez.

clue.text: Meddle in what could be seen as inept role

indicators.note: the letters could be seen differently, rearranged, as another word

explanation.surface: Interfering in a part one plays badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlope is to intrude into others' affairs, to interfere.

clue.text: Brilliant strike by criminal

parts.note: to lam is to beat or strike
bent is slang for crooked, criminal

explanation.surface: A dazzling blow delivered by a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent means softly glowing or flickering, luminous, as with brilliance.

clue.text: Stern warning in Olympic city provided with sensitivity

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympic Games
tact is sensitivity in dealing with others

explanation.surface: A firm caution issued tactfully in an Olympic host city.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading someone the riot act is a British idiom from the 1714 Riot Act, read to disperse crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a severe reprimand, as in reading someone the riot act.

clue.text: Sort of business caught losing heart totally in disposition that's backward-looking

indicators.note: the whole construction looks backwards, read right to left
the remaining letters of caught go inside the word for disposition

parts.note: a mood is a disposition or frame of mind

indicators.note: the word loses its whole heart, every inner letter, keeping only its ends

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A firm, caught out and heartless, stuck in nostalgic mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart totally' leaves CT from CAUGHT; 'in' puts it in MOOD, giving MOCTOD, which 'backward-looking' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot-com is a company trading mainly on the internet, a type of firm.

clue.text: Hemmed in by protest, a Tory is one prepared to leave things behind

definitions.text: one prepared to leave things behind

indicators.note: the letters are hemmed in by the surrounding words, enclosed in their run

explanation.surface: A Conservative surrounded by protesters is ready to walk away.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator makes a will, bequeathing property to be left after death.
